print_orientation: vertical, dispense end (Z=0) on the build plate

pauses.name: Solenoid + back-mounted ERM insertion (v3.2 co-located vibration source)
pauses.part: Adafruit #412 JF-0530B solenoid (9.6 × 19 × 22 mm) with Adafruit #1201 ERM disc (Ø10 × 2.7 mm) epoxied to its rear face
pauses.instructions: v3.2 co-locates the ERM with the solenoid so ERM vibration couples through the steel solenoid body → plunger → bore wall, instead of dissipating through PLA bulk as in v3. (1) BEFORE pause: epoxy the Ø10 × 2.7 mm ERM disc flat onto the back face of the JF-0530B body (the non-plunger end), leads dressed alongside the solenoid leads. (2) Pause printer at z = 19.9 mm. The -X face now exposes a pocket whose mouth is at x ≈ -45.2 mm (the boss outer face) and whose bottom is at x = -20.0 mm. Pocket length is solenoid_body_l + erm_disc_thk + 0.5 mm slip = 25.2 mm. (3) Insert the solenoid+ERM stack as a unit, ERM-first (against the pocket back wall at x = -45.2). The solenoid plunger points +X through the Ø5 plunger channel toward the bore. The fired plunger tip lands at x = -13.0 mm — 0.5 mm short of the auger OD at x = -12.5 mm — so the plunger TAPS the rotating tube without crushing it. (4) Route the four leads (two ERM + two solenoid) out through the 2.5 × 3 mm wire-egress slot on the back face of the -X boss. (5) Resume to lock the stack in place. Wired to the Bonnet: ERM → PWM (continuous fine vibration, low amplitude), solenoid → MOSFET (impulsive tapping, high amplitude).

install_after_print.name: Heat-set inserts
install_after_print.instructions: Press heat-set brass inserts: 4× M3 (Ø4.0 × 5.5 mm deep) into the e-bay lid corner holes (v3.2: now 4.25 mm in from each outer edge so the hole is centered in the 8.5 mm flange — was 6.0 mm in v3, which left only ~0.5 mm of wall to the lid opening and risked blow-out); 4× M3 into the new servo bracket flange on the +Y face; 4× M2.5 (Ø3.6 × 4.5 mm) into the stepper top plate (23 × 23 mm pattern); 4× M2.5 into the Pi standoffs on the +Y inner wall of the e-bay.

install_after_print.name: Servo external bracket install (v3.2 — cantilevered horn)
install_after_print.instructions: v3.2 NOTE: the v3 'rear bushing socket on -Y for both-sided horn support' has been REMOVED — a stock HD-1810MG horn is only 5–10 mm tall and could not span the ~60 mm gap to the -Y face (Edison P0). The horn now cantilevers in the Ø8 mm pass-through, as on any standard servo install. (a) Bolt the servo case to the 4 M3 heat-set inserts in the bracket flange on the +Y face; the servo case sits 2 mm proud of the chassis via the Ø16 mm airgap standoff ring (cooling airflow). (b) The servo horn output spline drives through the Ø8 mm pass-through into the chassis interior. (c) Connect horn linkage to the dispense-end mechanism. If a longer load path or bending support is needed in future revisions, an external dual-bearing servo block (mounted to the +Y face) is a cleaner option than a chassis-side rear bushing.

install_after_print.name: Pi Zero 2 W mount
install_after_print.part: Pi Zero 2 W on the +Y inner wall of the e-bay
install_after_print.instructions: Bolt the Pi Zero 2 W flat onto the 4 standoffs on the +Y inner wall of the bay (58 × 23 mm pattern, M2.5 into heat-sets). Orient the board so the mini-HDMI / micro-USB OTG / micro-USB power connector edge faces the -Z bay-floor cable slot (cables exit downward toward the desk).

install_after_print.name: Adafruit Stepper Bonnet stack
install_after_print.part: Adafruit Stepper Motor Bonnet (~65 × 30 × 15 mm) on Pi GPIO
install_after_print.instructions: Press the Bonnet onto the Pi GPIO 2 × 20 header. Bonnet drives the servo (PWM), solenoid (MOSFET), and the back-mounted ERM (PWM via logic-level). The Bonnet's onboard stepper driver is unused for the auger drive in v3 (see Tic 500 entry).

install_after_print.name: Pololu Tic 500 stepper controller (v3: USB-only, no GPIO clash)
install_after_print.instructions: v3 explicitly avoids the Bonnet GPIO contention reported in the v2 Edison review. VHB-tape (3M VHB 5952) the Tic 500 flat against the -X internal sidewall of the e-bay with its micro-USB port facing -Z (toward the bay floor cable slot). The Tic 500 talks to the Pi via micro-USB only — it does not sit on the GPIO header, so the Bonnet has the GPIO to itself. Stepper leads enter the bay through the +X wall grommet at z = 152 mm and land directly on the Tic 500 screw terminals.

install_after_print.name: DRV8825 stepper driver carrier (alternate)
install_after_print.instructions: VHB-tape the DRV8825 onto the +X internal sidewall of the e-bay. Optional fallback driver if not using the Tic 500 — wire to the Bonnet's STEP/DIR breakout pins.

install_after_print.name: E-bay lid
install_after_print.instructions: Print the matching lid (70 × 80 × 2.5 mm with 4 M3 clearance holes at the corners) separately and bolt to the heat-set inserts. v3 lid opening is 53 × 63 mm so the 8.5 mm flange comfortably accommodates the corner inserts. v3.2: clearance-hole pattern moved to 4.25 mm in from each outer edge (matching the chassis-side insert pattern).

install_after_print.name: Stepper + coupler install (top, v3.2 — Ø7 spindle)
install_after_print.part: NEMA 11 11HS18-0674S stepper + ST-FC01 5–5 mm coupler (auger side may need a 7–5 mm coupler instead)
install_after_print.instructions: v3.2 spindle change: auger spindle is now Ø7 mm × 24 mm (was Ø5 in v3) — fixes PLA cantilever bending stress (Edison P1). Chassis spindle pass-through bored to Ø8 mm (z = 250–258) below the full Ø19 coupler chamber. (1) Drop the auger in from above so its Ø7 spindle pokes through the spindle pass-through into the open coupler chamber. (2) Use a 7–5 mm shaft coupler (instead of the ST-FC01 5–5) so the larger auger spindle bore mates with the stepper's Ø5 D-shaft. Alternatively, embed a Ø5 steel rod axially down the spindle (pause printer at the spindle-base layer, drop in the rod, resume) and keep the ST-FC01 5–5. (3) Tighten the two coupler grub screws via the two Ø3.5 mm access ports on the +X face. (4) Bolt the stepper to the top plate with 4 × M2.5 into the heat-set inserts (23 × 23 mm pattern, Ø22 pilot pass-through). (5) Route the 4 stepper leads down the +X vertical wire slot and into the e-bay through the Ø5 grommet on the +X external wall of the e-bay at z = 152 mm.

wiring.summary: All four electrical lead groups (ERM, solenoid, servo, stepper) terminate inside the -Y e-bay. v3.2: ERM and solenoid share the same wire-egress slot out the back of the -X boss (ERM is now glued to solenoid back face). Servo + solenoid + ERM land on the Bonnet (PWM/MOSFET). Stepper lands on the Tic 500 (USB-connected, no GPIO clash).

paths.from: Back of solenoid (-X boss outer face, z=15)
paths.via: Out the -X boss rear wire-egress slot together with solenoid leads → around bottom of chassis → into e-bay lid opening
paths.to: Bonnet PWM output (3 V via logic-level) — fine continuous vibration

paths.via: Out the -X boss rear wire-egress slot → around bottom of chassis → into e-bay lid opening
paths.to: Bonnet MOSFET output (5 V) — impulsive tapping

paths.via: Around top of chassis → over the airgap ring → into e-bay lid opening
Down the +X vertical wire slot → through the Ø5 grommet on +X e-bay external wall at z=152 → directly to the Tic 500 screw terminals
paths.to: Tic 500 A1/A2/B1/B2 (USB-connected to Pi, no GPIO clash with Bonnet)

M3.count: 4 (e-bay lid corners, 4.25 mm inset) + 4 (servo bracket flange on +Y)

bore_breach_zones.summary: v3.2 keeps the v3.1 Ø5 round plunger channel (much smaller leak path than v3's 6 × 2.5 slot) and the same Z separation from the servo horn axle.

solenoid_plunger_kinematics_v3_1.summary: Plunger fired-tip lands tangent to the auger OD with a 0.5 mm safety gap — the plunger TAPS the rotating tube; it does not crush it. Unchanged in v3.2 (the back of the pocket grew by erm_disc_thk and the boss grew by the same amount, so the pocket BOTTOM and plunger reach are identical to v3.1).

v3_2_changes: ERM relocated from +X mid-tube embedded pocket to the BACK face of the solenoid (epoxied to solenoid rear during print pause). Vibration now couples through the steel solenoid body → plunger → bore wall instead of dissipating through PLA. ERM provides fine continuous vibration; solenoid provides coarse impulsive tapping.

Solenoid pocket length extended from 22.5 mm to 25.2 mm and the -X boss thickness grew from 7.5 mm to 10.2 mm (both +erm_disc_thk) so the back-mounted ERM disc fits behind the solenoid. Pocket bottom and plunger reach are unchanged.
Old +X mid-tube ERM pocket and its wire-egress slot DELETED.

Servo 'both-sided horn support' rear bushing socket (-Y face, Ø3.2 × 4 mm) REMOVED — a stock HD-1810MG horn is only 5–10 mm tall and could not span ~60 mm to the socket (Edison P0). Horn now cantilevers in the Ø8 pass-through.
E-bay lid heat-set inset reduced from 6.0 mm to 4.25 mm so the Ø4 hole is centered in the 8.5 mm flange instead of sitting 0.5 mm from the lid-opening edge (Edison P1).

Auger spindle bumped from Ø5 × 24 mm to Ø7 × 24 mm to address PLA cantilever bending stress at the coupler interface (Edison P1: Ø5 puts bending stress ~39 MPa, above PLA Z-direction ˜30 MPa yield; Ø7 drops to ˜14 MPa). Chassis spindle pass-through bored to Ø8 mm (was Ø6).
Schema bumped to v5 for the new solenoid_back_face_x_mm and erm_disc_x_range_mm fields.
v3_1_changes: Solenoid plunger reach corrected: external -X boss (7.5 mm) fully encloses the 22 mm body; Ø5 circular plunger channel replaces the 6 × 2.5 mm rectangular through-slot; fired-tip stops 0.5 mm short of the auger OD (clean tap, no crush). See solenoid_plunger_kinematics_v3_1.
Local bore wall pad (Ø12 × 2 mm) added around the plunger channel mouth to spread impact load over more PLA.
Schema bumped to v4 for the new bore_breach.solenoid_breach.shape and solenoid_plunger_kinematics_v3_1 sections.
v3_changes: Auger ↔ coupler spindle gap fixed: auger now extends with Ø5 × 24 mm spindle (auger script). Chassis has Ø6 mm pass-through (z=250–258) below the Ø19 coupler chamber.

Servo no longer embedded in a PLA tomb. External bracket on +Y with airgap standoff ring (2 mm), 2 ventilation slots, 4 M3 heat-sets, Ø8 mm horn-axle pass-through, and a Ø3.2 mm rear bushing socket on -Y for both-sided horn support.
E-bay lid heat-set holes moved to a thicker flange (lid opening shrunk from 63 × 75 to 53 × 63; flange grew from 3.5 mm to 8.5 mm).
Solenoid pocket rotated 90° so the 22 mm plunger axis is now along X (radial toward the bore), matching the tap-slot direction.
Stepper wire grommet relocated to the e-bay +X external wall (drilled through 2.5 mm of e-bay wall only) so the wires actually reach the Tic 500.
Solenoid bore-breach moved to z=10–20; servo horn axle at z=46–54. No overlap (25.9 mm clear gap).
Tic 500 GPIO clash with the Bonnet resolved by routing the Tic 500 over USB only (micro-USB port facing the bay floor cable slot).
notes: Pause Z is in millimetres along the chassis Z axis (matches the CadQuery script). Layer index = round(z_mm / layer_height_mm) at 0.2 mm; rescale if you slice differently. The user has chosen to leave the auger as a rotating-as-one-body design (no internal helix actually metering powder); this is acknowledged as a non-functional auger in the geometric sense but is preferred over PLA-on-PLA rubbing. Auger height (auger_tube_length) remains the single parameter to adjust for build-plate Z limits. v3.2 collapses two pause-pauses (separate solenoid + ERM) into a single pause because the ERM is now physically mated to the solenoid before insertion.
